R0005.title: Promotional Activity Cheating
R0005.definition: Using large numbers of accounts to complete platform promotional activities for profit.
R0005.description: After obtaining a large number of platform accounts, automatically completing platform promotional activities (including check-ins, tasks, red packet grabbing, coupon collection, flash sales, group buying, etc.). Account sources typically include bulk registration by black market operators (R0030), credential stuffing (R0032-001), credential cracking (R0032), or purchasing from black markets. Completing activities requires process automation capabilities (R0001).
R0005.influence: Exploits platform promotional benefits and prevents legitimate users from participating in activities.

references.title: What Does Promotional Activity Cheating Mean?

observables: Accounts engage in high-value promotional activities such as check-ins, coupon claims, and flash sales in a concentrated burst after a seasoning period
The same device fingerprint or IP is tied to many accounts repeatedly completing the same activity task sequence
Withdrawal and ordering behavior from participating accounts clusters within a short window before the activity ends
Accounts show extremely low retention and repurchase rates after completing activities, exhibiting pure arbitrage characteristics

R0005-001.title: Bulk Fake Account Manipulation
R0005-001.definition: Using large numbers of accounts to perform likes, favorites, shares, comments, etc. to influence platform ranking metrics and profit.
R0005-001.description: After obtaining a large number of platform accounts, automatically performing likes, favorites, shares, comments, and other functions to influence platform ranking metrics, enabling unfair competition and profit. Account sources typically include bulk registration (R0030), credential stuffing (R0032-001), credential cracking (R0032), or purchasing from black markets. Requires process automation capabilities (R0001).
R0005-001.influence: Manipulates platform ranking and recommendations through fake positive ratings and engagement volume, enabling unfair competition and crowding out legitimate seller exposure.

references.title: What Is the Purpose of Fake Followers? How to Remove Fake Followers?

observables: Likes, comments, and shares are triggered in a concentrated burst by large numbers of accounts within a short window, with mechanical timing
Engagement accounts show highly homogeneous registration times, device fingerprints, and IP ranges
Comment content is identical or templated, lacking genuine relevance to product details
Engagement volume on the target product/content spikes abnormally within a short window and then drops rapidly

R0005-002.title: Fake Viral Referral
R0005-002.definition: Using large numbers of accounts to complete referral, recommendation, and viral growth activities to fraudulently claim rewards for profit.
R0005-002.description: Also called 'new user acquisition cheating'. After obtaining a large number of platform accounts, automatically completing referral and recommendation tasks for profit. Account sources typically include bulk registration (R0030). Requires process automation capabilities (R0001).
R0005-002.influence: Siphons referral and viral-growth reward funds, inflates marketing costs, pollutes invitation-relationship data, and squeezes the rights of genuine users.

references.title: Governance Path for Advertising-Promotion Cyber Black-Grey Crime
Running a Viral Marketing Campaign? Don't Overlook the Anti-Cheating Component

observables: Within the referral chain, large numbers of invited accounts share clustered registration times and a common device fingerprint origin
Invited accounts stop being active immediately after completing the assist action, with no subsequent genuine usage behavior
Inviters and invitees share shipping addresses, payment accounts, or mobile-number ranges
Referral reward claims surge explosively within a short window right after the activity launches
